CODE_TEMPLATES.expectedFix: SELECT id, type, created_at FROM events WHERE user_id = %s ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 100
CODE_TEMPLATES.fixHint: Select only needed columns and add LIMIT 100
Replace the loop with a single findAll query using userId

CODE_TEMPLATES.issue: Cache set with no TTL — keys never expire
CODE_TEMPLATES.fixHint: Use setex with a 3600 second (1 hour) TTL

CODE_TEMPLATES.expectedFix: try { result = await conn.query(...); } finally { conn.release(); }
CODE_TEMPLATES.fixHint: Add try/finally block to release the connection after use

CODE_TEMPLATES.issue: No retry logic — single failure causes error
Committing inside loop — massive write amplification
CODE_TEMPLATES.expectedFix:
db.executemany("INSERT INTO processed (data) VALUES (%s)", [(e,) for e in events])
db.commit()
CODE_TEMPLATES.fixHint: Move commit outside the loop and use executemany for batch insert

CODE_TEMPLATES.issue: Sequential async calls that could run in parallel
CODE_TEMPLATES.fixHint: Use Promise.all to run independent async operations in parallel

CODE_TEMPLATES.issue: Sequential DB calls inside a loop
CODE_TEMPLATES.fixHint: Replace the sequential loop with Promise.all for parallel fetching

MULTI_CHOICE_TEMPLATES.question: DDoS attack detected. What is the FIRST action to take?

options.text: Enable WAF rate limiting and geo-blocking to filter malicious traffic
Scale up all app servers to absorb the attack traffic
Take the site offline until the attack stops

MULTI_CHOICE_TEMPLATES.question: Credential leak detected in logs. Best immediate response?

options.text: Rotate all affected credentials and revoke active sessions immediately
Wait for the security team to investigate before acting
Block the IP that accessed the leaked credentials

MULTI_CHOICE_TEMPLATES.question: Traffic spike is 3× normal. App utilization is at 95%. Best action?

options.text: Enable autoscaling and add 3 more app instances to absorb load
Enable maintenance mode to reduce traffic
Increase database connections to handle the extra queries

MULTI_CHOICE_TEMPLATES.question: DB replica lag is 45 seconds and rising. What causes this and how do you fix it?

options.text: Primary is under write-heavy load — tune max_wal_senders and replication slots
Network partition between primary and replica — restart both servers
Replica is out of disk space — promote it to primary immediately

MULTI_CHOICE_TEMPLATES.question: Cache hit rate dropped from 85% to 40%. Most likely cause?

options.text: Cache TTLs are too short or a noisy-neighbour is evicting hot keys via LRU
Too many concurrent reads are overwhelming the cache server
The application is not sending the correct cache headers

MULTI_CHOICE_TEMPLATES.question: Workers are consuming jobs but results are never saved. Root cause?

options.text: DB connection pool exhausted — workers acquire a connection but it times out before commit
Queue is full — jobs are being dropped before workers pick them up
Worker memory limit reached — jobs are silently killed mid-execution

MULTI_CHOICE_TEMPLATES.question: SSL certificate expires in 2 hours and auto-renewal failed. Best response?

options.text: Issue an emergency cert via certbot --force-renewal and deploy it immediately
Temporarily disable HTTPS and serve over HTTP until the issue is resolved
Wait for auto-renewal to retry in 6 hours as per the renewal schedule

MULTI_CHOICE_TEMPLATES.question: API gateway is returning 502 errors. What do you check first?

options.text: Check if upstream app servers are healthy — 502 means gateway cannot reach them
Restart the API gateway itself — it likely has a configuration error
Check client-side rate limiting — clients may be sending malformed requests

MULTI_CHOICE_TEMPLATES.question: Disk is at 98% on the primary database server. What should you NOT do first?

options.text: Delete the database data directory to free space immediately
Identify and remove old WAL segments and archive logs safely
Move the largest tables to a separate volume via tablespace

MULTI_CHOICE_TEMPLATES.question: A single Kubernetes pod is in CrashLoopBackOff. Fastest diagnostic step?

options.text: kubectl logs <pod-name> --previous to see the crash reason before restart
kubectl delete pod <pod-name> to force a clean restart
kubectl describe node to check if the node has resource pressure
